Commercial shipping

A professional industry—not one single course or job.

Merchant vessels carry cargo, energy and goods across global trade routes. Deck teams navigate and manage cargo; engine teams operate and maintain machinery; ratings support safe day-to-day work; catering teams support life onboard.

Your route depends on where you start. Academic subjects, age, medical fitness, recognised training and certification can all matter. Salary advertisements alone cannot tell you which route is available.

Pathways explained simply

Your starting qualification shapes the options.

This is a simplified orientation. Always check current DG Shipping guidelines and recognised institution criteria.

After Class 10

GP Rating route

An entry pathway toward deck and engine rating work. Recognised pre-sea training, medical fitness and certification requirements apply.

  • Hands-on operational work
  • Progression requires sea service and further eligibility
  • Verify institution and certification independently
Check GP Rating Eligibility
After Class 12 PCM

DNS deck officer pathway

Diploma in Nautical Science is associated with a deck cadet/officer route, combining required education, training and sea-service stages.

  • Academic and medical standards apply
  • Sea-time and later examinations matter
  • Understand sponsorship claims carefully
Discuss the Deck Route
After Class 12 PCM

BSc Nautical Science

A degree pathway oriented toward nautical education and a future deck officer career, followed by required sea service and certification.

  • Degree is not the final officer licence
  • Institution recognition must be verified
  • Plan for medical and sea-time requirements
Compare Nautical Pathways
After Class 12 PCM

Marine engineering route

A technical officer pathway focused on propulsion, machinery and engine-room operations, with recognised education and subsequent certification.

  • Suited to mechanical and technical aptitude
  • Academic and physical standards apply
  • Progression involves sea service and examinations
Explore Engine Officer Guidance
Ranks & progression

The career ladder is earned in stages.

Titles vary by company and vessel. Advancing generally requires the right documents, sea service, examinations and performance.

Deck department

  1. 01
    Deck rating / cadet

    Learn safe routines, seamanship, cargo or navigation support under supervision.

  2. 02
    Junior / third officer

    Take defined watchkeeping, navigation and safety responsibilities after required certification.

  3. 03
    Second & chief officer

    Manage broader navigation, cargo, safety and team responsibilities with experience.

  4. 04
    Master / Captain

    Hold overall command, subject to required certification and appointment.

Engine department

  1. 01
    Engine rating / cadet

    Support machinery maintenance, housekeeping and safe engine-room routines.

  2. 02
    Junior / fourth engineer

    Take assigned machinery and watch duties after required training and certification.

  3. 03
    Third & second engineer

    Handle increasing technical, maintenance and team responsibilities.

  4. 04
    Chief engineer

    Lead engine department operations, subject to certification and appointment.

Reward vs reality

The sea can build a career. It also asks for trade-offs.

Entry rating or trainee earnings are often discussed around ₹20,000–₹60,000 per month while onboard, with officer pay varying substantially by rank and vessel. These are indicative industry ranges, not guaranteed National Global Academy outcomes.

Always distinguish monthly onboard pay from annual take-home income, and ask whether leave is paid.

Potential rewards

  • Structured rank and skill progression
  • Global exposure and specialist experience
  • Saving potential during contracts
  • Technical and leadership development

Important trade-offs

  • Long periods away and contract uncertainty
  • Medical and certification obligations
  • Watch duties, fatigue and physical work
  • Competitive entry and market cycles
Avoid the scam traps

A recognised course is not the same as a guaranteed ship job.

Verify the institution and course through current official sources. Ask who receives each payment and obtain receipts. Be cautious of “sponsorship” that requires unexplained cash, agents who refuse employer verification, or anyone promising a joining date without a documented process.

NGA’s role is training and career guidance, not a promise of employment.

Straight answers

Merchant Navy questions, answered plainly.

Make your next decision with verified information.

Is Merchant Navy a government job?

Usually no. Most seafarers work for private shipping companies or managers on commercial vessels. “Merchant Navy” describes an industry, not a single government employer.

Which is better: GP Rating or DNS?

They are different entry routes. GP Rating prepares for rating-level work; DNS is associated with a deck officer pathway for eligible candidates. Compare academic eligibility, medical standards, costs and long-term goals.

Can I become an officer after GP Rating?

Progression may be possible subject to applicable sea service, education, examinations and certification rules. It is not automatic; verify the current route with official requirements.

Is there always a salary between contracts?

Many seafaring roles pay while onboard or under contract, not necessarily during shore leave. Contract terms vary, so budget for waiting and leave periods.

How do I verify a maritime institute?

Use current official DG Shipping information and directly confirm the institution, course and certification. Do not rely solely on a consultant’s screenshot or verbal assurance.
